tag_patterns.line: SIZE - SERVICE - SPEC - NUMBER - INSULATION. Example: 6-P-A9A-1001-HC.
tag_patterns.equipment: First letter is the component type, next two letters the modifier, then the unique number. ABJ 1000 = Atmospheric vessel, Tank, item 1000. C 1000 = Compressor with no modifier.
tag_patterns.safety_device: ISA letters then an optional device number. PSV = Pressure Safety Valve. PSH2 = Pressure Safety High, device 2. USV is an underwater safety valve; SSV is the wellhead surface safety valve.

instrument_bubbles.mounting: no extra mark = remote and accessible to the operator; a horizontal line = field mounted; a dashed horizontal line = remote and inaccessible; a double horizontal line = auxiliary mount accessible; a dashed double line = auxiliary mount inaccessible
instrument_bubbles.shared_display: A box with a defined letter is a shared display; a box with a defined number is a shared control

risk_matrix.note: On the sheet, consequence index 1 is Catastrophic and likelihood index 1 is Likely. The engine renumbers so level 6 is the worst consequence and the highest likelihood.

severity.Incidental: Safety: workforce minor injury such as first aid; public no impact. Health: minor illness or limited effect, treatment not necessary; public no impact. Environment: localised or short-term effect on habitat, species or media.
severity.Minor: Safety: one or more minor injuries, not severe; public one or more minor injuries such as first aid. Health: mild to moderate illness, some treatment, medically manageable; public illness with limited or no impact, treatment not necessary. Environment: localised long-term or widespread short-term impact.
severity.Moderate: Safety: one or more severe injuries including permanently disabling injuries; public injuries that are not severe. Health: serious illness or severe adverse health effect needing a high level of treatment; public illness or adverse effect with moderate functional impairment. Environment: localised but irreversible habitat loss, or widespread long-term effects.
severity.Major: Safety: workforce 1 to 4 fatalities; public one or more severe injuries including permanently disabling injuries. Health: serious illness or chronic exposure with significant life shortening; public serious illness or severe adverse effect needing a high level of treatment. Environment: significant, widespread and persistent change in habitat, species or media.
severity.Severe: Safety: workforce multiple fatalities (5 to 50); public multiple fatalities (1 to 10). Health: workforce fatalities (5 to 50) or serious illness or chronic exposure with significant life shortening; public 1 to 10 serious illnesses or chronic exposures with significant life shortening. Environment: persistent reduction in ecosystem function on a landscape scale, or significant disruption of a sensitive species.
severity.Catastrophic: Safety: workforce multiple fatalities (more than 50); public multiple fatalities (more than 10). Health: workforce more than 50 fatalities, or serious illness or chronic exposure resulting in fatality or significant life shortening; public more than 10 serious illnesses or chronic exposures resulting in fatality or significant life shortening. Environment: loss of a significant portion of a valued species or of effective ecosystem function on a landscape scale.

likelihood.Likely: Conditions can reasonably be expected to occur in the life of the facility.
likelihood.Occasional: Conditions may allow the consequences to occur at the facility during its lifetime, or the event has occurred within the Business Unit.
likelihood.Seldom: Exceptional conditions may allow the consequences to occur within the facility lifetime, or the event has occurred within the OPCO.
likelihood.Unlikely: Reasonable to expect the consequences will not occur at this facility. It has occurred several times in the industry, but not in the OPCO.
likelihood.Remote: Has occurred once or twice within the industry.

legend: Scores 1, 2, 3 and 4: short-term interim risk reduction is required. A long-term risk reduction plan must be developed and implemented.
Score 5: additional long-term risk reduction is required. If no further action can reasonably be taken, seek SBU management approval to continue the activity.
Score 6: risk is tolerable if reasonable safeguards and management systems are confirmed in place and consistent with the Risk Mitigation Closure Guidelines.
Scores 7, 8, 9 and 10: manage the risk. No further risk reduction is required. Risk reduction stays at management or team discretion.
